title: How can two products be found without long multiplication?
description: Ninety eight times one hundred two and forty five times fifty five are each rewritten around a round number, as one number minus a gap times the same number plus the gap. The board then shows one square minus another square. Keeko thinks the short and the extra cancel to give a round square, and a small case with nine and eleven breaks that.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two numbers sit the same gap either side of a middle number, their product is the middle number squared take away the gap squared. Watch for students who think the short and the extra cancel, so that the product is the square of the middle number.

source: Calculate 98 × 102 and 45 × 55 using the difference of two s
video_script.why: The child can multiply two brackets, but has not yet seen that numbers the same gap either side of a middle number multiply to one square minus another.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as the middle number minus or plus the gap, then use the rule for a sum times a take away.
video_script.anchor: the book's two products, ninety eight times one hundred two and forty five times fifty five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says ninety eight is two short of a hundred and one hundred two is two over, so they cancel and the answer is ten thousand. The square of the gap is still taken away.
video_script.payoff_line: Ninety eight times one hundred two is nine thousand nine hundred ninety six.

final_answer.spoken: nine thousand nine hundred ninety six and two thousand four hundred seventy five

maths_rules: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − ab + ba − b² = a² − b²
slip: 100² = 10000; the gap square 2² = 4 is forgotten
video_script.design: One idea: numbers the same gap either side of a middle number multiply to the middle square take away the gap square. The two products stay on the board. Keeko's wrong idea is that the short and the extra cancel.

<bookmark mark='products'/>Find ninety eight times one hundred two, and forty five times fifty five.

narration: <bookmark mark='lines'/>Your book shows a pattern. Nine times nine minus one times one is ten times eight.
Eight times eight minus six times six is fourteen times two.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>In each line, ten is nine plus one and eight is nine minus one. Fourteen is eight plus six and two is eight minus six.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>This gives the rule, eigh squared minus b squared is eigh plus b times eigh minus b.
<bookmark mark='why'/>It is true because the two middle terms in the expansion cancel.

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, ninety eight is one hundred minus two, and one hundred two is one hundred plus two.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the rule, ninety eight times one hundred two is one hundred squared minus two squared.

beats.on_screen: 100² = 10000 and 2² = 4; then 10000 − 4 waits to be worked out

marks.take: 10000 − 4 is written, not yet worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='squares'/>Step two, put in the values. One hundred squared is ten thousand, and two squared is four.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Then we take four away from ten thousand.

marks.rule: the rule turns the line into 50² − 5²

beats.colours: the sum in one colour, the take away in another
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, forty five is fifty minus five, and fifty five is fifty plus five.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the rule, forty five times fifty five is fifty squared minus five squared.

beats.on_screen: 50² = 2500 and 5² = 25; then 2500 − 25 waits to be worked out

marks.take: 2500 − 25 is written, not yet worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='squares'/>Step four, fifty squared is two thousand five hundred, and five squared is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Then we take twenty five away from two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Ninety eight times one hundred two is nine thousand nine hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Forty five times fifty five is two thousand four hundred seventy five.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ninety eight is two short of a hundred, and one hundred two is two over.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Keeko says the short and the over cancel, and the answer is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Let us try a smaller case. Nine is one short of ten, and eleven is one over.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Nine times eleven is ninety nine, not one hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The short and the over do not cancel. The square of the gap is still taken away.
